~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Step 5: Creating resistance surface
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#Resistance sutface for Etosha wet/dry 
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(here)

# 0. Configuring
# ------------------------------------------------------------
pop_label   <- "etosha"
target_year <- 2020 #non-static covariates using this single year 
 
gee_folder      <- here("data", "500m_data")
lc_dist_folder  <- here("data", "ESACCI_LCCS", "lc_dist_2")
evi_folder      <- here("data", "500m_data", "EVI data")
model_folder    <- here("outputs")
out_folder      <- here("outputs", "resistance_surfaces")
dir.create(out_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
 
lc_types    <- c("cropland", "grassland", "shrubland", "tree_cover", "urban", "water_rivers")
wet_months  <- c(1:4, 11:12)
dry_months  <- c(5:10)
 
crop_extent <- ext(12.5, 25.5, -21.5, -16.5) 
target_res  <- 0.0045 # 500m in degrees 
template    <- rast(crop_extent, resolution = target_res, crs = "EPSG:4326")

# 1. Load fitted SSF modles
# ------------------------------------------------------------
 
m0_etosha_wet <- readRDS(here("outputs", "m0_etosha_wet.rds"))
m0_etosha_dry <- readRDS(here("outputs", "m0_etosha_dry.rds"))

# Define the area where the Etosha SSF is valid to only mask the used area and remove extrapolated pixels 

ele_trk_extract_etosha <- readRDS(here("outputs", "ele_trk_extract_etosha.rds"))

etosha_pts <- ele_trk_extract_etosha |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(case_) |>  # used steps only (not random steps)
  select(x2_, y2_) |>
  drop_na()

etosha_vect <- vect(etosha_pts, geom = c("x2_", "y2_"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

#Using a conevex hull and buffer to allow for movement just beyond the outermost GPS fix 
valid_area <- buffer(convHull(etosha_vect), width = 5000)

# 2. Build static covariate raster (seaonal)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_static_stack <- function() {
 
  static_files <- c(
    # CHECK: SSF extraction used "core_dist_rast_500m.tif" (no "_new"). If the two files differ, the betas are being applied to the wrong values. Use the same file as extraction.
    core_dist  = file.path(gee_folder, "core_dist_rast_500m_new.tif"),
    fence_dist = file.path(gee_folder, "fences_dist_rast_500m.tif"),
    road_dist  = file.path(gee_folder, "roads_distance_rast_500m.tif")
  )
 
  r_list <- map(static_files, ~ project(rast(.x), template, method = "bilinear"))
  r_stack <- rast(r_list)
  names(r_stack) <- names(static_files)
 
  terrain_r <- rast(file.path(gee_folder, "terrain_rast_500m.tif"))
  terrain_r <- project(terrain_r, template, method = "bilinear")
  
  c(r_stack, terrain_r)
}

#Linear feature stack 
build_linear_stack <- function() {
 
  linear_types <- c("hydrorivers", "kaza_vet_fences", "roads")
  linear_folder <- here("data", "Linear_features")
 
  r_list <- map(linear_types, function(feature) {
    fp <- file.path(linear_folder, paste0(feature, "_linear_500m.tif"))
    project(rast(fp), template, method = "near")
  })
  r_stack <- rast(r_list)
  names(r_stack) <- paste0(linear_types, "_linear")
 
  r_stack
}

# 3. Build land-cover distance stack, average across year 
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_lc_dist_year <- function(year = target_year) {
 
  paths <- setNames(
    file.path(lc_dist_folder, paste0("dist_", lc_types, "_", year, ".tif")),
    lc_types
  )
  paths <- paths[file.exists(paths)]
 
  missing_lc <- setdiff(lc_types, names(paths))
  if (length(missing_lc) > 0) {
    warning("Land-cover distance rasters missing for ", year, ": ",
            paste(missing_lc, collapse = ", "))
  }
 
  r_list <- map(paths, ~ project(rast(.x), template, method = "bilinear"))
  r_stack <- rast(r_list)
  names(r_stack) <- paste0(names(paths), "_dist")
  r_stack
}

# 4. Build EVI mean surface for given season
# ------------------------------------------------------------
 
build_evi_year <- function(season, year = target_year) {
 
  fp <- if (season == "dry") {
    file.path(evi_folder, paste0("evi_dry_", year, ".tif"))
  } else {
    # wet season files span year boundaries: evi_wet_(yr-1)_(yr).tif
    file.path(evi_folder, paste0("evi_wet_", year - 1, "_", year, ".tif"))
  }
 
  if (!file.exists(fp)) {
    stop("EVI raster not found for ", season, " ", year, ": ", fp)
  }
 
  r <- project(rast(fp), template, method = "bilinear")
  names(r) <- "evi"
  r
}

# 5. Build population mean surface across years
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_world_pop_year <- function(year = target_year) {
  world_pop <- rast(file.path(gee_folder, "worldPop_comb_img_500m.tif"))
  world_pop <- project(world_pop, template, method = "bilinear")
 
  layer_idx <- year - 1999  #matches indexing used in the SSF extraction script
  if (layer_idx < 1 || layer_idx > nlyr(world_pop)) {
    stop("No world_pop layer available for year ", year)
  }
 
  pop <- world_pop[[layer_idx]]
  names(pop) <- "world_pop"
  pop
}

# 6. Full covariate stack for one season
# ------------------------------------------------------------

build_covariate_stack <- function(season, year = target_year) {
  static_stack  <- build_static_stack()
  linear_stack  <- build_linear_stack()
  lc_stack      <- build_lc_dist_year(year)
  evi_stack     <- build_evi_year(season, year)
  pop_stack     <- build_world_pop_year(year)
 
  full_stack <- c(static_stack, linear_stack, lc_stack, evi_stack, pop_stack)
  full_stack
}

# 7. Predict linear predictor / SSF from model coefficients (REVISED)
# -----------------------------------------------------------

predict_ssf_surface <- function(model, covariate_stack) {
 
  #fit_clogit() function wraps the model inside '$model', so extract '$model' here to get correct coefficients 
  betas <- coef(model$model) #pulls out statistical weights calculated by SSF
  betas <- betas[!is.na(betas)]  # Remove any variables that failed to calculate (ignore NA values) 
  
#compare names of varibales in the model against the names of the map layers provided. Creates a list of any required varibales that are missing from the map. If there is something missing, triggers an error and prints what is missing
  missing_in_stack <- setdiff(names(betas), names(covariate_stack))
  if (length(missing_in_stack) > 0) {
    stop("Model covariates missing from raster stack: ",
         paste(missing_in_stack, collapse = ", "))
  }
 
  #using name based indexing to prevent the wrong coefficient multiplying by the wrong variable. Retrieves corresponding layer and multiplies that entire layer by its matching scalar weight. 
  weighted <- lapply(names(betas), function(nm) covariate_stack[[nm]] * betas[[nm]])
  
  #sums all the weighted layers into a linear predictor 
  lp <- sum(rast(weighted))   #linear predictor surface
  names(lp) <- "linear_predictor"
  lp
  
}

# 8. Linear predictor to resistance surface
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lp_to_resistance <- function(lp, min_resistance = 1, max_resistance = 100, shape_parameter = 3,
                             clip = c(0.01, 0.99)) {
 
#Takes 1st percentile and 99th percentile values of preference scores and cuts any below or above this because extreme outliers
  q <- as.numeric(quantile(values(lp, na.rm = TRUE), probs = clip))
  lp_c <- clamp(lp, lower = q[1], upper = q[2])
  
  # Uses min max normalization to transform preferences into h, a scale running from 0 to 1 (0 = least selected habitat, 1 = most selected habitat)
  h <- (lp_c - q[1]) / (q[2] - q[1])
  
  # Non-linear Exponential Resistance Transformation
  # As h approaches 1 (high selection), resistance approaches min_resistance 
  # As h approaches 0 (lower selection), resistance rises toward max_resistance
  # shape_parameter controls curvature (larger = resistance drops off faster as habitat improves)
  # the (1 - exp(-c*h)) / (1 - exp(-c)) term is already scaled to 0-1, so resistance hits exactly min/max without a separate rescaling step.
  resistance <- max_resistance -
    (max_resistance - min_resistance) *
    ((1 - exp(-shape_parameter * h)) / (1 - exp(-shape_parameter)))
  
  names(resistance) <- "resistance"
  
  resistance
 
}

#9. Run 
# ------------------------------------------------------------
run_resistance_pipeline <- function(model, season, pop_label, valid_area) {
  message("Building covariate stack for ", pop_label, "-", season)
  cov_stack <- build_covariate_stack(season) 

  message("Predicting linear predictor surface")
  lp <- predict_ssf_surface(model, cov_stack) #Calculate habitat selection 
  
  # mask before transforming: the quantile clipping and normalization in lp_to_resistance() should only see pixels the model can be trusted on.
  message("Masking to area where the SSF is valid")
  lp <- mask(lp, valid_area)
  
  # lp should span a modest range, not tens/hundreds of units
  print(global(lp, c("min", "max", "mean", "sd"), na.rm = TRUE))

  message("Converting to resistance surface")
  resistance <- lp_to_resistance(lp)

  out_path <- file.path(out_folder, paste0("resistance_", pop_label, "_", season, ".tif"))
  writeRaster(resistance, out_path, overwrite = TRUE)
  message("saved: ", out_path)

  resistance 
}

#Run
resistance_etosha_wet <- run_resistance_pipeline(m0_etosha_wet, "wet", pop_label, valid_area)
resistance_etosha_dry <- run_resistance_pipeline(m0_etosha_dry, "dry", pop_label, valid_area)

#Visualize
plot(resistance_etosha_wet, main = "Etosha Wet Season Resistance Surface")
plot(resistance_etosha_dry, main = "Etosha Dry Season Resistance Surface")
plet(resistance_etosha_wet, col = rev(terrain.colors(100)), tiles = "OpenStreetMap")
```

```{r}
cov_stack <- build_covariate_stack("wet")
betas <- coef(m0_etosha_wet$model); betas <- betas[!is.na(betas)]
cs <- mask(cov_stack[[names(betas)]], valid_area)

# per-term contribution (beta * value), so you can see which one steps at ~14.9
contrib <- rast(lapply(names(betas), function(nm) cs[[nm]] * betas[[nm]]))
names(contrib) <- names(betas)
plot(contrib, nc = 4)          # look for the layer with the vertical edge

# west vs east of the seam, ranked by size of the jump
w <- ext(14.3, 14.8, -19.2, -18.4); e <- ext(15.1, 15.6, -19.2, -18.4)
jump <- data.frame(
  term = names(betas),
  west = global(crop(contrib, w), "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[, 1],
  east = global(crop(contrib, e), "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]
)
jump$diff <- jump$east - jump$west
jump[order(-abs(jump$diff)), ]

# which layer is NA over the pan
global(is.na(cs), "sum")
```
